claims.feature: glimpsed threads of a larger tapestry
claims.claim: Hromic (via Wikipedia) describes the usual sense of far more in the background than told, glimpsing a few shining threads in a larger tapestry.
claims.source: Wikipedia: The Last Light of the Sun (Reception citing Hromic, Dusmann)
claims.quote: glimpsing a few shining threads in a larger tapestry

claims.feature: weak magic keyed to romance sources
claims.claim: Ringel notes magic in Arbonne is weak, no wizard's duels, in keeping with the scarcity of pagan marvels in real medieval romances.
claims.source: Faye Ringel, 'Kay's Provence: From Arbonne to Ysabel' (ICFA 2009 / Anticipation 2009 paper)

claims.claim: Ringel reads Arbonne and Ysabel as portraying Provence as a palimpsest where older history bleeds through into the present.
claims.source: Faye Ringel, 'Kay's Provence: From Arbonne to Ysabel' (ICFA 2009 / Anticipation 2009 paper)
claims.quote: a palimpsest of time and space

claims.claim: Ringel quotes Bethune that events separated by centuries are often collapsed into a single era while only the cultural milieu is kept.
claims.source: Faye Ringel, 'Kay's Provence: From Arbonne to Ysabel' (ICFA 2009 / Anticipation 2009 paper)
claims.quote: often collapsed into a single era

claims.claim: Ringel shows Kay transforming troubadour poems (Peire Vidal, Bernart de Ventadorn) into the in-world song of the title.
claims.source: Faye Ringel, 'Kay's Provence: From Arbonne to Ysabel' (ICFA 2009 / Anticipation 2009 paper)
claims.quote: transforms these and other troubadour poems

claims.claim: Tarantino's essay characterises Kay's writing as elegiac and gently melancholy, turning on memory, continuity and the consequences of conduct (read via summary; quote withheld).
claims.source: Bob Tarantino, 'The fantastic fiction of Guy Gavriel Kay', C2C Journal (2016-09-07)

claims.claim: Randall states that in the passage narrating Darien's death in The Darkest Road the sentences are short and the description concrete.
claims.quote: Sentences are short, description is concrete.

claims.claim: Randall describes the tone of that same Darien death passage as matter-of-fact.
Randall reads the passage narrating the departure of Arthur, Lancelot and Guinevere as a deliberate reach for rhetorical high style, in contrast with the plain Darien passage.
claims.quote: the language here is an obvious attempt at rhetorical

claims.claim: Randall explains the elevated register of the Arthurian departure scene as a consequence of who perceives it, not of the event's importance.
claims.quote: because it is perceived by minds capable of comprehending magnificence

claims.claim: Randall counts twenty-six different agents of focalization in The Fionavar Tapestry.
claims.quote: employs twenty-six different agents of focalization
claims.page: opening section, before 'Assimilating the Secondary World'

claims.claim: Randall counts twenty-one shifts of focalization in the eighth chapter of The Summer Tree.
Randall counts eighty-seven shifts of focalization across Darien's search for Rakoth, with Darien himself the focalizant only nine of those times.
claims.quote: the narrative shifts focalization eighty-seven times

claims.claim: Randall argues that Kay's shifts of focalization delay the unfolding of the story as well as advancing it.
claims.quote: the shifts delay the unfolding of the story

claims.claim: Randall argues the reader must assemble Kay's secondary world by inference from the successive focalizations rather than from direct exposition.
claims.quote: Our task is to piece together the world by understanding the focalizations.
